subject: Climate & Environment
title: The US Clean Air Act
description: A fast breakdown of The US Clean Air Act for builders.

hook.text: In 1970, rivers were catching fire and smog choked American cities. Congress acted fast.

buildup.text: The Clean Air Act set national limits on six key pollutants and created the EPA to enforce them.

discovery.text: Since 1970, the six major pollutants dropped 78% — while the US economy grew 285%.

twist.text: The law's benefits outweigh its costs by an estimated 30 to 1 ratio.

climax.text: It prevented an estimated 230,000 early deaths per year by 2020.

punchline.text: The best investment America ever made was cleaning the air.

quiz.question: By how much did the six major pollutants drop since the Clean Air Act?

details.summary: The US Clean Air Act of 1970 and its 1990 amendments set national air-quality standards, regulated tailpipe and smokestack emissions, and introduced the cap-and-trade program for acid rain. It is credited with preventing hundreds of thousands of premature deaths.
details.whyItMatters: The Clean Air Act demonstrates that regulation can dramatically improve public health while the economy grows. Its cost-benefit ratio exceeds 30-to-1 by EPA estimates.
takeaways: Six criteria pollutants are regulated under national standards
The 1990 amendments added acid rain and ozone-depleting substance controls
Benefits have exceeded costs by more than 30 to 1

faq.question: What are the six criteria pollutants under the Clean Air Act?
faq.answer: They are particulate matter, ground-level ozone, carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, and lead. The EPA sets National Ambient Air Quality Standards for each and states must develop plans to meet them.

faq.question: Has the Clean Air Act hurt the US economy?
faq.answer: No. US GDP has roughly tripled since 1970 while regulated pollutant emissions fell by over 70 percent. The EPA estimates the Act's health and productivity benefits exceed its costs by a ratio of more than 30 to 1.
